title: Integrating adaptive human behavior into epidemic models with large language models
abstract: arXiv:2608.29535v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Infectious disease transmission is shaped by patterns of human interaction, which adapt as epidemic conditions change. Capturing these context-dependent behaviors remains a fundamental challenge for epidemic models. Here, we recast this challenge by using large language models (LLMs) to represent adaptive human behavior within mechanistic epidemic models. We operationalize this idea through Generative Adaptive Behavioral Layer for Epidemics (GABLE), which adapts LLMs to infer behavioral responses to epidemic and policy conditions and translates them into age-structured contact matrices coupled to a mechanistic epidemic model. Applied to COVID-19 in France, GABLE reproduced responses in population mixing and age-specific contact structures that remained epidemiologically informative. translated_title: 利用大语言模型将自适应人类行为整合到流行病模型中
translated_abstract: 传染病传播受到人类互动模式的影响，而这些模式会随着疫情形势的变化而调整。捕捉这些依赖情境的行为仍然是流行病模型面临的一项根本性挑战。在本研究中，我们通过使用大语言模型（LLMs）来表示机制性流行病模型中的自适应人类行为，从而重新构建了这一挑战。我们通过“流行病生成式自适应行为层”（GABLE）实现了这一想法，该方法使大语言模型能够推断对疫情和政策条件的行为反应，并将其转化为与机制性流行病模型相耦合的年龄结构接触矩阵。应用于法国的COVID-19疫情时，GABLE再现了人群混合行为以及年龄特异性接触结构的变化反应，且这些反应在流行病学上仍具有参考价值。在短期预测中，LLM生成的接触矩阵优于由真实世界流动性数据推导的流动性驱动矩阵，其中优势最为明显的是
tldr: 该研究提出GABLE框架，利用大语言模型推断人群对疫情和政策条件的行为反应并生成年龄结构接触矩阵，与机制性流行病模型耦合后，在法国COVID-19短期预测中的表现优于基于真实流动性数据的接触矩阵。
en_tdlr: The study introduces GABLE, a framework that uses large language models to infer adaptive human behavioral responses to epidemic and policy conditions, generating age-structured contact matrices coupled with mechanistic epidemic models, which outperform mobility-driven matrices in short-term COVID-19 forecasting in France.
